references.page_title: How Coding Agents Fail Their Users: A Large-Scale Analysis of Developer-Agent Misalignment in 20,574 Real-World Sessions
references.notes: 8 authors total (only first confirmed by name); v1 submitted 28 May 2026. Observational study of 20,574 sessions from 1,639 repos, misalignment defined via developer pushback; 7 recurring forms incl. following rules and bounding actions. Abstract says constraint violations 'grow in share' over time; it does NOT say they are among the most common failures. Abstract does not mention context loss as a cause (annotation axes: form, cause, cost, resolution). Do not claim either without reading the full text.

references.page_title: Push Your Agent: Measuring and Enforcing Quantitative Goal Persistence in Long-Horizon LLM Agents
references.notes: Hash is of the arXiv abs page; alphaxiv URL also opened (HTTP 200, no redirect, body sha256 c17b119ec5f5a2be59a03535803b90a581a34a2a56a8369a8cc5801362d83f46) but arXiv is the canonical copy; cite the arXiv URL. 5 authors; submitted 22 May 2026. Studies quantitative goal persistence (keep working until a verifier confirms enough distinct valid items). Does not study prohibitions or compaction per abstract. The name 'PushBench' was not confirmed from the title; check the full text before using it.

references.page_title: Technical Report: Evaluating Goal Drift in Language Model Agents
references.notes: 4 authors; submitted 5 May 2025. Setup: goal given in system prompt, then environmental pressure from competing objectives; measures drift over long contexts (>100k tokens); all models drifted, scaffolded Claude 3.5 Sonnet best; drift rises with context length. Title on page has the 'Technical Report:' prefix.

references.page_title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
references.notes: 7 authors; submitted 6 July 2023. Abstract re-read 2026-11-04 (arXiv abs page, curl body sha256 af63ac4b31d2d47748f3ad62081349ff820ca488c577888c8b0289545915c275): performance is often highest when relevant information is at the beginning or end of the input context and degrades significantly when it is in the middle, even for explicitly long-context models; tasks are multi-document question answering and key-value retrieval.

Vendor docs, no authors; year is retrieval year. Quote: 'Project-root CLAUDE.md survives compaction: after /compact, Claude re-reads it from disk and re-injects it into the session. Nested CLAUDE.md files in subdirectories and rules with paths: frontmatter load again on demand.' Also: CLAUDE.md is treated as context, not enforced configuration; docs recommend a PreToolUse hook to block actions. Note the sentence is scoped to project-root CLAUDE.md; do not generalize.

Vendor docs. Page text is 286k chars; WebFetch read the first 100k only. Events listed: SessionStart, Setup, SessionEnd, UserPromptSubmit, UserPromptExpansion, Stop, StopFailure, PreToolUse, PermissionRequest, PermissionDenied, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, PostToolBatch, SubagentStart, SubagentStop, TaskCreated, TaskCompleted, TeammateIdle, PreCompact, PostCompact, PreModelSwitch, PostModelSwitch, Elicitation, ElicitationResult, InstructionsLoaded, ConfigChange, CwdChanged, DirectoryAdded, FileChanged, WorktreeCreate, WorktreeRemove, Notification, MessageDisplay. PostCompact exists. SessionStart matcher values: startup, resume, clear, compact, fork (compact fires after compaction). PreCompact/PostCompact matchers: manual, auto. PreToolUse output: {hookSpecificOutput:{hookEventName:'PreToolUse',permissionDecision:'allow|deny|ask|defer',permissionDecisionReason:...}}, optional updatedInput and additionalContext; alternatively exit code 2 blocks with stderr as reason.
